provisionChecks.result: Actual hierarchy and minimum-protection routes read

Actual workplace performance is unverified.

provisionChecks.result: Actual binding dynamic floor and national technical route assessed
provisionChecks.evidence: Benzene0.66 mg/m³/0.2 ppm and skin notation after the expired5 April 2026 transition. GefStoffV §7(8)(2) expressly requires the current 2004/37 Annex III values after their transposition deadline, alongside national AGWs. TRGS 900/910 relevant selected rows/notes were actually read as separate, sometimes more protective or risk-based routes. Fractions and reference periods are part of the quantitative floor; notation-related information and controls must also be assessed through the national classification, instruction and technical-note routes. The word “limits” alone is not treated as automatic incorporation of every non-numeric notation. A risk concentration alone is not silently substituted for the binding floor. This is not an exposure/practice audit.

provisionChecks.evidence: S.I. 632/2025 Regulation 7 replaces principal Regulation 3(2): express application of more favourable general Act, chemical-agent and CMR safeguards. Current S.I. 122/2024 as amended by 128/2026 was independently read.
S.I. 632 Regulation 23 replaces Schedule 1 with six fibrous silicates classified as CLP category 1 A. Current asbestos Code Schedule 1 repeats the correct CAS numbers and types.

S.I. 632 Regulation 9(1) expressly prioritises removal in risk assessment. S.I. 589/2010 Regulation 3(d), replacing principal Regulation 15, requires a written plan and removal before other demolition except where that increases exposure risk.

S.I. 632 Regulation 9(2) limits principal Regulation 5(b) to disapplication of Regulation 11, removing old health/register exemptions. Regulation 11 now also contains the permit, creating the separately documented qualified scope concern.

S.I. 632 Regulation 13 requires training certificates, notification, work plan, risk assessment and prior permit number. Regulation 25 and Schedule 3 include worker lists, certificates, latest health assessment, site particulars, methods, decontamination, waste, air exchange and equipment.

S.I. 632 Regulation 11 requires technically lowest exposure, dust suppression, source suction, sedimentation, decontamination, confinement, cleaning and sealed transport/waste. Principal Schedule 2 hygiene now applies without the old exception.

S.I. 632 Regulation 12 requires operational-phase, personal representative samples and competent sampling/analysis. Principal Regulation 10(1) is triggered by an initial assessment at or above the limit, whereas current Code page 6 describes risk-based sampling. Equivalent effect for lower assessed levels remains legally inconclusive; no separate public outcome claim.

S.I. 632 Regulation 12 specifies electron microscopy or an equally/more accurate alternative now; current Code page 7 still recognises competent WHO 1997 phase-contrast microscopy. The EU electron/thin-fibre duty is not due until 21 December 2029. No current missed future deadline is inferred; the combined route remains an interpretation question.

Binding principal Regulation 6, replaced by S.I. 632 Regulation 10, incorporates the latest Code. The complete eight-page Code Schedule 1 sets the current 0.01 fibres/cm³ eight-hour TWA from 21 December 2025.

Actual Code Schedule 1 provides future 0.01 fibres/cm³ including fibres thinner than 0.2 µm and the 0.002 alternative from 21 December 2029. Future national choice and administration are not certified or treated as a current omission.

S.I. 632 Regulation 15 replaces principal Regulation 13(1): immediate stopping on exceedance or disturbance of previously unidentified asbestos, followed by cause identification and remedy. Retained Regulation 13(2) bars resumption until adequate protection.
S.I. 632 Regulation 15(2) limits respirator use and requires regular breaks appropriate to physical/climatic conditions, with consultation.

S.I. 632 Regulation 14 replaces principal Regulation 12(1): for pre-31 December 2004 premises, obtain owner/employer/register information or a competent survey before work; share survey information with another employer on request.
S.I. 632 Regulation 16 requires individually adjusted, fit-tested PPE and a sealed enclosure under mechanical extraction. Current Code page 6 also requires fit testing.

S.I. 632 Regulation 17 replaces principal Regulation 15(10), requiring written site clearance before other activities. The full Regulation 15 in S.I. 589/2010 retains competent independent analysis as appropriate.

S.I. 632 Regulations 19/28 and entire Schedule 7 cover initial, regular and needs-based theory/practice; competent trainers; five certificate fields; all subjects; profession-specific adaptation; and additional demolition/removal equipment training.

Principal Regulation 11(1)(a)(iv)/(b), inserted by S.I. 632 Regulation 13, requires a prior permit number and public list, but is expressly subject to Regulation 5(b). The whole of Regulation 11 is disapplied for qualifying intact low-risk removal. HSA issues a permit per notification. See qualified private candidate ie-asbestos-low-risk-permit-exception; no actual unpermitted work or harm shown.

S.I. 632 Regulation 21 replaces principal Regulation 24 with all medically diagnosed asbestos occupational diseases and doctor reporting. Regulation 27 adds lung/larynx/ovarian cancers and non-malignant pleural disease; Regulation 22 removes the low-risk register exemption. Actual principal Regulations 20–25 health and 40-year record routes were read.
Commission reviews require no separate national rule.

S.I. 632 was signed 17 December 2025 and states commencement on 21 December; notice was published 30 December. Current Code also commenced 21 December. Official histories updated 13 October 2026 list only the 2010 and 2025 amenders and show 632 unaffected. Historical Commission notification/performance was not audited.
